Article Title: ‘We should not waste our energy’: Manu Bhaker urges Indian athletes to look beyond Asian Games chaos
Article Text:
Manu Bhaker (AFP Photo)

‘We should not waste our energy’

Manu Bhaker to lead India's contingent as flag bearer

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Shooting ace Manu Bhaker has urged her fellow Indian athletes to put the organisational issues surrounding the Asian Games behind them and focus on competition, saying the continental showpiece represents a “once in a lifetime opportunity and experience”.The build-up to the Games in Japan has been marred by complaints from athletes and officials of several participating countries, including India, over cramped accommodation, organisational mismanagement and long travel times between hotels and training venues.With criticism mounting over the arrangements, Bhaker called on the Indian contingent not to allow the problems to distract them from their performances.“To all my fellow athletes from India, we will have some issues. I saw a couple of issues circulated in social media and people telling me these are the issues,” Bhaker said in a video message posted by the Indian Olympic Association.“Regardless of whatever the issues we have, this is probably a once in a lifetime opportunity and experience. We have to make sure that we enjoy the time rather than complaining,” she added.Bhaker, a double Olympic medallist, said Indian athletes had worked too hard to reach the Asian Games to allow the organisational difficulties to consume their attention.“We have prepared the best we can and so we must try to perform the best we can. We have worked so hard to be here and we should not waste our energy in pointing out that this is not right and that is not right. Medal may come or not, that is another story, but we must give our best.”The 24-year-old has been given another significant responsibility at the Games after being named one of India's two flag bearers for Saturday's opening ceremony.Bhaker created history at the Paris Olympics in 2024 when she became the first athlete from Independent India to win two medals at a single edition of the Olympic Games. She won bronze in the women's individual 10m air pistol and mixed team 10m air pistol events.The Asian Games will also carry a strong personal significance for Bhaker, who is competing at the continental event for the third time.“When I came to know of this (being chosen as one of the flagbearers), I had flashbacks of my earlier days. When I started, I never thought I would reach this far one day. It's definitely feeling proud and honoured,” she said.“I was just 16 years old when I competed in the Asian Games in 2018. This is my third Asian Games. I was in Palembang (Indonesia) in 2018 and so could not attend the ceremony.”Bhaker recalled that her late coach Jaspal Rana had allowed her to attend opening ceremonies of multi-sport events only when she was a flag bearer, given the tight competition schedule for shooters.“The first time I attended the opening ceremony was in the Commonwealth Games and I was like if I am the flagbearer I will attend because my (then) coach Jaspal (Rana) sir said he will allow me attend the ceremony if I am the flagbearer, otherwise not. Since our matches usually start just a day after the opening ceremony, it becomes hectic for us.“So in opening ceremonies, I am either a flagbearer or I watch the ceremony on television.”Earlier on Saturday, seasoned kabaddi player Pawan Sehrawat replaced shot-putter Tajinderpal Singh Toor as the other Indian flag bearer after Toor was unable to attend the ceremony because he did not have the required ceremonial kit in his luggage.
Article Summary: Shooting ace Manu Bhaker has urged her fellow Indian athletes to put the organisational issues surrounding the Asian Games behind them and focus on competition. The build-up to the Games in Japan has been marred by complaints over cramped accommodation, organisational mismanagement and long travel times between hotels and training venues. Bhaker, a double Olympic medallist, has been given another significant responsibility at the Games after being named one of India's two flag bearers for Saturday's opening ceremony.

Article Title: ‘Both trophies will come’: BCCI’s big update on Asia Cup trophies India refused to take from Naqvi
Article Text:
Indian women's cricket team and Mohsin Naqvi

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Asia Cup trophies won by India's men's and women's teams remain in Dubai, but BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia has assured that both pieces of silverware will eventually make their way to the board's headquarters in Mumbai.Saikia confirmed the development after the BCCI's 95th Annual General Meeting in Mumbai on Friday, although he stopped short of specifying when the trophies would arrive. The men's and women's teams had both declined to receive the Asia Cup trophy from Asian Cricket Council president Mohsin Naqvi, leaving the silverware at the ACC headquarters in Dubai."Asia Cup trophies, we hope it will come one day," Saikia said in Mumbai on Friday after the BCCI's 95th Annual General Meeting.“I will not give you a timeline, but I can assure you that both the trophies will come up and land up in this BCCI head office at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai,” he added.The latest development follows India's women's team refusing to attend the trophy presentation after beating Sri Lanka in the Women's T20 Asia Cup final last week. Harmanpreet Kaur 's side did not appear at the presentation ceremony with Naqvi on the dais, while a similar situation had unfolded after India's men's team won the Asia Cup last year.The women's team instead conducted its own medal presentation after the final, with BCCI secretary Saikia and vice-president Rajeev Shukla presenting Nandni Sharma with the fielding medal. The official ceremony later saw Naqvi present the runners-up cheque to Sri Lanka.Saikia had already made the BCCI's position clear a day after the women's final, describing the decision not to accept the trophy from Naqvi as a "firm institutional decision".“Our position had been communicated to the ACC in advance that the Indian team would not participate in the trophy presentation under the circumstances. Given the circumstances and the sentiments prevailing in the country, the BCCI felt that it would not be appropriate for the team to receive the trophy in the proposed manner,” Saikia told news agency PTI.“This was a firm institutional decision, reflective of the position we have maintained, and was not directed at the players, the tournament or the sport,” he added.The issue could have implications beyond the Asia Cup, with India and Pakistan both competing at the Asian Games in Japan. The Asian Games cricket tournament is being conducted under the ACC, while both Indian teams are among the contenders for gold. The possibility of Naqvi being involved in a medal presentation could therefore become another point of attention.Saikia's latest comments also come with Naqvi's current term as ACC president approaching its scheduled conclusion in April 2027. Whether he receives an extension will depend on the support of ACC members.The strained cricketing relationship between India and Pakistan has remained evident since the Pahalgam terror attack, with players from the two teams having refused to shake hands with each other in subsequent encounters.
Article Summary: India's men's and women's cricket teams refuse to accept Asia Cup trophies. Asian Cricket Council president Mohsin Naqvi left the silverware in Dubai. But BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia says the trophies will eventually arrive in Mumbai. It follows India's women's team refusing to attend the trophy presentation.

Article Title: The leap that began with a dare: A childhood challenge, a swollen toe and the 8.07m jump that made TC Yohannan an Asian Games legend
Article Text:
TC Yohannan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Over five decades have passed, but Thaduthuvila Chandapillai Yohannan, the genial octogenarian, recounts that day in Tehran with the enthusiasm of a five-year-old.It’s the 1974 Asian Games and the then 28-year-old long jumper’s left toe is swollen. He walks onto the runway, taking painkillers.Yohannan’s first attempt lands at 7.25m. The pain shoots up and he takes more painkillers. The second one hits 7.8m and the third is a foul.On his fourth attempt, something clicks. He lands at 8.07m, a leap that would remain an Asian record for three decades.“As I was standing at the podium, with the national anthem playing in the background, I knew I had achieved something momentous,” he told TOI. Yohannan could not sleep that night, partly due to the swelling on his toe. The national anthem was still playing in his mind.As the Asian Games begin in Japan today, Yohannan’s gold medal assumes significance. Kerala will be represented by 28 athletes, continuing the state’s rich sporting tradition.Long before he rewrote the record books in Tehran, there was a stream in Maranadu, a village in Kollam and a dare that almost cost his friend a glass of lemonade.“I was eight or nine and we used to walk 3km to school. My friend Georgekutty dared me to jump across the stream. I jumped and landed in it and he ran away. I went home and told my father, T Chandapillai, what happened,” recalled Yohannan. The father took his son to the stream and asked him to jump. “This time, I cleared it. My father rewarded me with a glass of buttermilk. Unknowingly, this was the start of my athletics career. My father was my inspiration,” he said with a laugh. In school, Yohannan would participate in every event, be it sprints, long jump or high jump.The youngest of six brothers, Yohannan’s athletics journey ran through a steel plant in Bhilai, where one of his elder brothers worked. He joined NCC and started turning up at the plant’s meets. “I once ran 100m in 10.6 seconds,” he said. A sports division officer at the plant, who was impressed, pointed him toward the long jump pit.Yohannan was just 5’9”, short by long jump standards. He made up for it with speed off the runway, a strong core and a leg extension that stretched every cm during take-off. “You must be quick and have strong abdominal muscles. I used to practice six hours a day,” he said.After securing a diploma in mechanical engineering in 1970, he joined TELCO (now Tata Motors) where sports officer Suresh Gujarati used innovative methods like setting up high hurdles at the end of the runway to help Yohannan gain extra height during flight.He jumped using the hand-and-arm technique, arms sweeping through the air to fight the forward rotation that take-off creates, buying the body just enough balance to stretch during landing. Today’s jumpers mostly favour the hitchhiking style, legs cycling through the air like a person running on nothing. “The sport has moved on. I was the product of an earlier generation,” he said.At the 1976 Montreal Olympics, he couldn’t touch the qualifying mark of 7.8m and finished 16th, with a foot ailment flaring at the worst-possible moment. “If I had matched my Tehran timing, I would have bagged a bronze at Montreal,” he said.In 1978, while training at Patiala’s National Institute of Sports, he jumped into a pit that should have been filled with sand and sawdust. But rain had made it soggy. “As I jumped, the ground underneath me sank. My ligament was ruptured,” he recalled.He was admitted to a local hospital that evening. Tatas stepped in and moved him to Gangaram Hospital in Delhi. “A team of doctors worked on me. I spent over six months on crutches. They said I would never be able to run or do long jumps again. I was only 32. I felt I had more to achieve as an athlete,” he rued.TELCO moved him to the sales department, where he built a second career, before he shifted permanently to Kochi in 1983 with his family.Looking back, Yohannan never expected his record to last 30 years. “Murali Sreeshankar has the height and gift to touch 8.5m if conditions align. Ancy Sojan, who broke Anju Bobby George’s 22-year-old national record, can clear 7m. They are medal prospects in Japan,” he said.When asked why ex-cricketer Tinu didn’t follow in his father’s footsteps, he joked: “Tinu was not willing to work hard, which is why he became a fast bowler.” Seventy years after he fell into a stream, climbed out and set a record, Yohannan has still not lost his zest for life.
Article Summary: Thaduthuvila Chandapillai Yohannan won a gold medal at the 1974 Asian Games in Tehran. His leap of 8.07m remains an Asian record for three decades. He was just 5’9”, short by long jump standards, but made up for it with speed off the runway.

Article Title: Why was the Asian Games 2026 flag-hoisting ceremony delayed?
Article Text:
The Indian national flag among those of participating nations at the venue during the official welcome and flag-hoisting ceremony ahead of the 20th Asian Games, in Nagoya, Japan. (PTI Photo/Arun Sharma)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

‘THERE IS MISMANAGEMENT’

NAGOYA: The clock is ticking for Japan, most unusually. A country synonymous with punctuality and quiet efficiency has been struggling with the clock in its role as Asian Games host.On Friday, the flag-hoisting ceremony for six contingents — India, Yemen, North Korea, Palestine, Chinese Taipei and Timor-Leste — was delayed by more than an hour because of what organisers described as “miscommunication” between the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) and the Games organising committee (ANAGOC).The ceremony at Garden Pier was scheduled for 1:30 pm local time but was initially pushed back by 20 minutes, following which the ceremonial band began playing. However, just before the contingents were due to take the stage, they were asked not to proceed and were made to wait before eventually being sent back to the waiting area.No Indian athlete was in attendance, but chef de mission Sahdev Yadav and deputy chefs de mission Sharath Kamal, Anjali Bhagwat, Lijo Thottan and Alaknanda Ashok were present.Initially, the delay was attributed to the late arrival of the chief guest.An ANAGOC official later offered a different explanation.“The communication between the Olympic Council of Asia executive board and the organising committee was not well, that’s why this happened. It’s not like somebody delayed the ceremony,” the official said.India’s chef de mission Yadav, meanwhile, sought to assure that efforts were being made to ensure athletes were not inconvenienced by the organisational issues that have plagued the Games in the build-up.“Initially there were problems, but we have booked extra hotel rooms. Our officials are at the airport to sort out issues. There is mismanagement, but in a Games on this scale it happens, but we are focused on solving the problem of our athletes. We have booked about 18 extra hotel rooms and are now looking at 10 more,” Yadav told reporters.
Article Summary: The flag-hoisting ceremony for India, Yemen, North Korea, Palestine, Chinese Taipei and Timor-Leste was delayed by more than an hour. Organisers blamed'miscommunication' between the Olympic Council of Asia (OCA) and Games organising committee (ANAGOC)

Article Title: Asian Games 2026: ‘My biggest bet would surely be the doubles’ - Neha Aggarwal Sharma on India’s table tennis medal hopes
Article Text:
For Neha Aggarwal Sharma, the difference between this Indian team and the one she was part of at the 2014 Asian Games is hard to miss.

Doubles carries the clearest medal opportunity

Men’s team has experience around Manav and Manush

The Manika Batra gap

Divyanshi and Syndrela lead the next generation

(Watch

Asian Games 2026

live and exclusive on Sony Sports Network and Sony LIV)

India’s 10-member table tennis contingent is already in Japan, with the Aichi-Nagoya competition for the event beginning on September 20. At the forefront are world No. 3 men’s doubles pair Manav Thakkar and Manush Shah, while India also has experience in Sathiyan Gnanasekaran and Harmeet Desai, and a younger group featuring Sreeja Akula, Yashaswini Ghorpade, Diya Chitale and Syndrela Das.For Neha Aggarwal Sharma, the difference between this Indian team and the one she was part of at the 2014 Asian Games is hard to miss.“I remember when I played at the 2014 Asian Games, we lost in the quarterfinals. We played against China. It was a close match.”“We lost a few others. I mean, we weren't really expected to win medals and it was okay. And now cut to 2026, if you look at, say, my sport, table tennis in particular, we are going in as the world number three in men's doubles,” Sharma told Timesofindia.com in an exclusive interaction facilitated by Sony Sports Network.12 years on, the expectation around Indian table tennis has changed. Sharma sees it not only in the rankings and results, but in how the players approach international competition.“The sort of improvement that India has seen is phenomenal. And I think that mindset shift is what is, to me as an athlete, what we need to see. And we are seeing now for India, Indian sports overall.”For table tennis specifically, however, Sharma is not suggesting the job is done.India has moved up the rankings, won at the WTT Feeder level and started collecting medals at Contenders. However, against China, Japan and Korea, the consistency is still missing.“We are winning, say, at the WTT level, we are winning feeders. We are now winning medals at the Contenders, we have had some good performances at the [WTT] Star Contenders as well. But I think we are not consistently beating China, Japan and Korea.“You would see one-off wins here and there. But for us to really bridge that gap, I think it is going to take another generation to do that,” assessed the 2008 Olympian.The strength of this Indian squad is spread across the doubles events, and for Sharma, that is where India can realistically challenge for medals and build towards the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028.“Firstly, we have to start building the narrative for mixed doubles and men's and women's doubles. Why? it is at the Olympics now, very simple. And even if you talk from LA perspective, these are the events which are our genuine medal chances.”“So, even, not to put pressure on Manav, Manush, Dia, Yashaswini, but genuinely we have chances,” quipped the former No. 1 ranked Indian paddler.India also has a recent Asian Games reference point in women’s doubles. Sutirtha Mukherjee and Ayhika Mukherjee had won a historic bronze at the 2022 Hangzhou Games.“Last time, if you recall, Suteertha and Ahika had won the bronze in the women's doubles. So that's one clear, clear medal chance,” said Sharma.The men’s team combines the current form of Manush and Manav with the experience of Sathiyan and Harmeet. Sathiyan has been a mainstay of Indian table tennis for more than a decade, and Sharma believes his experience can have a role in the team event.“Manush is in fantastic form. Manav has been doing great as well, and it is good to see Sathiyan back. He had a bit of a downfall the last two years, but very, very happy to see [him back] because his experience will count quite a lot from the team's perspective.”India’s women’s team, meanwhile, has a different task. Sharma recalled the previous Games, when India lost to Thailand in the round of 16.“I think this time, if we get past that round of 16, once you're in the quarterfinals, you'll have China, Japan, Korea and I think Hong Kong or Singapore, either of these four countries, depending on the draw. There it's anybody's game, in my opinion, so it is possible.”And she believes the men have the stronger team-event chance.“I do believe the men have a better chance in the team events than the women do.”But when asked where she would put her strongest medal call, Sharma went back to the doubles.“We can surely get medals in the team events as well. But my biggest bet would surely be the mixed doubles and men’s and women’s doubles events.”There is also a conspicuous absence from India’s women’s team. Manika Batra was left out of the Asian Games squad after not meeting the selection criteria, with her absence from domestic events meaning she did not feature in the TTFI’s national rankings. Batra publicly questioned the consistency and transparency of the selection process and sought a detailed explanation from the federation.It has left India without one of its most experienced women’s players for the Asian Games - and Sharma was careful not to let the selection row overshadow what the team taking the court in Japan can do.“Keeping the controversy aside, see, I think Manika has really asserted her position in world table tennis as somebody who can beat anybody at any time.”“You can see from 2018 onwards, that's when she rose. And till now, you keep seeing these one-off wins. And when we spoke about consistency, right? Like Manika has been able to consistently beat world top 20 players.”For Sharma, Batra’s value also comes from her ability to handle pressure and the way her presence can affect an opponent.“She is one player who performs well under pressure. You need those players in your team. Second, also similar is Sreeja.”But Sharma emphasised that the focus has to be on the players who will be in Japan.“We will miss Manika. But yes, players like her just boost the morale in a different way. Even from the opponent's perspective that, you know, somebody like her is there. But having said that, I just feel that let's not get into all of that.”“Let's focus on who we have. Sreeja is just fresh off of winning the feeder at Puerto Princesa. I think, even somebody like a Syndrela Das, she just plays her heart out.”There is a wider point to Sharma’s argument about the gap with China, Japan and Korea. India has had players such as Sharath Kamal and Manika Batra who could produce results at the highest level.Now, Sharma is looking at the teenagers coming through behind them - among them Divyanshi Bhowmick and Syndrela, two players she believes have the game and mindset to eventually challenge the best in Asia.Syndrela is already in Japan with the Asian Games squad; Bhowmick figures in Sharma’s assessment of the larger pipeline.“To build a generation of athletes, say, for example, a Divyanshi Bhowmick or a Syndrela Das, right, at respectively 15 and 17 years old, the sort of game that they have and the mindset that they have, they are really the ones who can consistently be there at the level where we can beat our top class of China, Japan, Korea.”Sharma pointed to the number of young Indian players now competing at WTT events.“Because I can already see the next crop coming up. Just the number of players that have increased in terms of participation. I mean, it's fantastic the number of players who are playing at the under-15 and under-17 level at the WTT levels.“They're spending from their own side and going and taking part in tournaments. It's heartening to see that.”And when asked which Indian table tennis players she was most interested in watching at the Games, Sharma returned to Syndrela and the men’s doubles pair.“In table tennis, I am very excited about... One is Syndrela Das. And second is for Manav and Manush to either get us the men's doubles. Or in the men's team, to see those wins.”
Article Summary: India’s 10-member table tennis contingent is already in Japan, with the Aichi- Nagoya competition for the event beginning on September 20. The strength of this Indian squad is spread across the doubles events, and for Sharma, that is where India can realistically challenge for medals and build towards the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028.

Article Title: 'Very important for captain and coach to be on your side': Abhishek Sharma on Shubman Gill-Gautam Gambhir backing
Article Text:
Abhishek Sharma (BCCI Photo)

Abhishek turns dead rubber into his night

India race to 100 in six overs

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Poll Vote & Share your view What was the most impressive part of Abhishek's innings? Fastest T20I century Number of sixes Consistency across the series 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Afghanistan collapse again

NEW DELHI: Abhishek Sharma believes the backing of captain Shreyas Iyer and head coach Gautam Gambhir has played an important role in allowing him to play his natural game.Abhishek made the most of that freedom on Thursday, smashing a record 30-ball century against Afghanistan in the third and final T20I in Delhi. His 108 off 34 balls, which included 11 sixes, helped India post 221/7 and complete a 3-0 series sweep with a 127-run win.The left-hander was named both Player of the Match and Player of the Series after finishing the three-match series with 209 runs.Speaking after his match-winning knock, Abhishek said the team culture and the support of the captain and coach have allowed him to express himself without worrying about failures."I've told in the first interview as well. We've been doing this last two years. One or two bad series won't define us as a batting department. We wanted to dominate throughout the whole year before the world cup no matter who the opposition is. I feel as a batter, sometimes you have up and downs. The most important thing is as a team we have to be together and support each other. That's how these innings happen," Abhishek said at thye post match presentation."I feel it's all dependent on my process before every series. It's very particular for me, against who I play and their bowlers. How I'm going to utilise the powerplay. Who's going to bowl the powerplay, the 7th over, the 8th over," he said."And the way I play, it's very important for the captain and the coach to be on your side. You have to get surety. I feel this is because of them as well. I feel I don't want to restrict any area. It's just watch the ball and play according to it. It's very simple from day one. I just want to express myself. Just see the ball and hit the ball. You can't be sure you'll be doing well all the time but the culture we've developed in our team is to dominate and it's been going well so far," Abhishek said.With India having already sealed the series, the third T20I was a dead rubber. Abhishek, however, ensured there was little doubt about where the spotlight would be. It was the first time in the series that India batted first and Abhishek immediately went after the Afghanistan attack. He brought up his fifty from just 16 balls and then completed his hundred in the ninth over.He reached 99 with a powerful pull off Abdullah Ahmadzai before taking a single to reach three figures. He then removed his helmet and celebrated with a seated meditation pose as the crowd rose to applaud him. His 108 came from only 34 balls and included 11 sixes and nine fours. It was the fastest T20I century by an Indian batter, beating Rohit Sharma's 35-ball hundred against Sri Lanka in 2017.It was also the fastest T20I hundred by a batter from a Test-playing nation against another Test-playing nation, surpassing Finn Allen's 33-ball century against South Africa earlier this year.Abhishek's attack gave India a flying start. India reached 100 without losing a wicket in the powerplay, their highest score in the first six overs of a T20 match.Afghanistan struggled to contain him from the beginning. Azmat Omarzai conceded 17 runs in the second over, while Fazalhaq Farooqi gave away 23 in the third.Captain Ibrahim Zadran turned to spin during the powerplay, but that did little to stop Abhishek. Sanju Samson also joined the attack, hitting two straight sixes off Mohammad Nabi before Abhishek cleared the boundary twice in the same over, which cost Afghanistan 29 runs.Samson, dropped on 22 at mid-off by Zadran, went on to score 50 off 35 balls for his second successive fifty-plus score.Abhishek's departure in the 10th over came with India on 142/1. India eventually finished on 221/7 after losing four wickets and scoring 37 runs in the final five overs.Afghanistan's batting once again failed to put India under pressure. They were bowled out for 94 in 14.1 overs, giving India a 127-run win.Nitish Kumar Reddy opened the bowling for India and conceded 15 runs in his first over before returning later to claim three wickets. Axar Patel removed Rahmanullah Gurbaz and Sediqullah Atal during the powerplay, while Jasprit Bumrah produced a sharp yorker to dismiss Darwish Rasooli. Yash Thakur then accounted for Ibrahim Zadran in the sixth over.Afghanistan were 47/4 at that stage and never recovered.Both teams will now head to the Asian Games
Article Summary: India beat Afghanistan by 127 runs in the third and final T20I in Delhi. Abhishek Sharma scored 108 off 34 balls, which included 11 sixes and nine fours. The left-hander was named both Player of the Match and Series. India won the three-match series 3-0.

Article Title: NE Inter State Badminton C’ship kicks off in Shillong after a decade as stars shine on opening day
Article Text:
Assam's Ashmita Chaliha (front) in Shillong on Wednesday

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: The two top-ranked players at the North East Inter State Badminton Championships – Assam’s Ashmita Chaliha and H. Lalthazuala of Mizoram – shone on the opening day with identical one-sided wins for their teams in respective matches at Jawaharlal Nehru Indoor Sports Complex in Shillong.While Chaliha, the world No. 41 and only Indian to win the Korea Masters, led Assam to a 3-0 win in a women’s team match against Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram’s former U17 national champion, Lalthazuala, was flawless in his team’s 3-0 victory over Tripura in their men’s team clash on Wednesday.It was, however, a disappointing start to the hosts’ campaign as Meghalaya lost their first matches in each of the four age categories in the team competition.But hosting the tournament after a decade and having more than 250 badminton players from across the northeast gathered in the Meghalaya capital for the four-day competition, the state has aims to use the match exposure to select the contingent for the team competition at National Games 2027, also to be hosted in Shillong at the same venue.“We do understand that champion is created from this kind of platform,” Wailadmiki Shylla, the minister of sports and youth affairs in the Meghalaya govt, said at the inauguration of the tournament that saw participation from all eight states of the northeast.Meanwhile, Chaliha was satisfied with the infrastructure and facilities available to the players at the tournament ahead of next year’s National Games, she highlighted the rise of grassroots talent across the region.In her message to the hosts’ shuttlers, who have not been able to gain the success of powerhouses like Assam and Mizoram, she said: “Enjoy what you play, give your absolute best on the court without taking the pressure of winning or losing, and the results will naturally follow.”In a reflection of the state’s desire to reach top level in Indian badminton, Shylla also announced a dedicated training stipend for Meghalaya’s final National Games team and said special provisions would be made under the Meghalaya Health Insurance Scheme to support treatment for sports-related injuries.
Article Summary: Assam's Ashmita Chaliha and H. Lalthazuala of Mizoram shone on the opening day of the North East Inter State Badminton Championships in Shillong. The two top- ranked players led their teams to identical one-sided wins for their teams. Meghalaya lost their first matches in each of the four age categories in the team competition.

Article Title: 'Make our fans proud': Dani Ramirez eyes win as East Bengal target Al-Shorta after historic ACL Two draw
Article Text:
Ramirez against Al Hussein

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: East Bengal’s Spanish attacker Dani Ramirez believes that his team’s stunning 2-2 draw at Jordanian champions Al Hussein SC will help them grow in confidence in Asia’s second-tier club football Ramirez scored one and provided assist to Anwar Ali’s goal as Antonio Lopez Habas’ team became the first Indian club to register a point in an away game in the rebranded AFC Champions League Two. It could’ve been more remarkable for them had they not conceded a goal at the death to let their 2-0 lead slip away.Ramirez, however, insisted after the match in Amman that they would go for a win when they host Iraq’s Al-Shorta in their next match at the Salt Lake Stadium on Oct 13."I hope we can win our second ACL Two group match against Iraq's Al-Shorta on 13 October in Kolkata, and make our fans proud.“We still need to improve in a few areas, and that introspection started in the dressing room right after the match. That said, this performance will give us a huge confidence boost, and we will carry these lessons into the next match,” Ramirez told the club’s media team.Only three foreigners, playmaker Mohammed Rashid and Croatian defender and debutant Diego Zivulic being the other two, were available for East Bengal ACL2 Group D opener.But they are likely to face Al-Shorta at home with the possibility of three more foreign attackers —Australia’s Chris Ikonomidis, Ivory Coast’s Ake Arnaud Loba and Polish striker Lukasz Zwoliński, being available for selection.“We played well as a unit (in Amman), and with our fans backing us at home, I am confident we can deliver a positive result,” Ramirez maintained.Al-Shorta are leading the Group D after the first-round action, following their 1-0 win over Oman’s Al Seeb.
Article Summary: East Bengal drew 2-2 at Jordanian champions Al Hussein SC in the AFC Champions League Two. Dani Ramirez scored one and provided assist to Anwar Ali’s goal. Antonio Lopez Habas’ team became the first Indian club to register a point in an away game.

Article Title: Things not looking good as India's elite men suffer three draws at Samarkand Olympiad; women beat Finland

Praggnanandhaa plays his first game at Olympiad 2026

Things are not looking too good for defending champions India at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.No. 52 seeds Indonesia held their own against the second seeds and eked out three draws, losing a game to only Nihal Sarin and went down by the smallest of margins (1.5-2.5) in the second round on Thursday.India’s celebrated elite men players, who largely play among fellow 2600-plus players and hence get rating protection even if they play out draws, seem to be found wanting in a street fight - an essence of sport where a fancied player has more at stake than the underdog. Therein lies the charm of the Swiss League and Olympiad.Nihal won with white pieces against Abdul Hafiz, a player about Elo 250 lower than him. R Praggnanandhaa, D Gukesh and Vidit Gujrathi could only draw with players about Elo 300 lower than them.India had rested Arjun Erigaisi after he lost in the opener and hence world champion Gukesh was promoted from the designated fourth board to the third on the second successive day.Pragg took the top board but could not breach the defence of Susanto Megaranto after five and a half hours and 79 moves.The top seeded India women’s team defeated Finland 3.5-0.5 with reasonable conviction but R Vaishali could not win on the top board and Divya Deshmukh flirted with danger before getting a semi-gift.Koneru Humpy was rested. Women’s 48th seeds Montenegro held second seeds Georgia 2-2.If top seed USA’s Levon Aronian’s creative risk-taking was punished with a draw in the opening round, his 23-year-old teammate Awonder Liang suffered defeat against IM Khuyagtsogt Itgelt of Mongolia in the second round.Former world champion Ding Liren, who is given the top board by China despite his recent troubles, messed up a sumptuous winning position with plenty of time in hand against Chile’s Rodrigo Vasquez Schroeder, and managing only half a point.Pakistan, who forfeited against Israel in the opener, presumably in protest against the conflict in Palestine, blanked Seychelles 4-0.Inclusivity is one of the stronger points at the Olympiad. The third edition of the Olympiad for People with Disabilities was held at the same venue.These players were given an extra half an hour each for each of the seven rounds to complete their games. Poland regained the gold that they had won in the inaugural edition.

Article Title: 'High chance we will bring home a medal': Yuvraj Sandhu confident ahead of Asian Games
Article Text:
​Yuvraj Sandhu

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Yuvraj Sandhu will be taking the long route to Japan. Back at 'sweet home' Chandigarh for five days, he has no time to rest after going through the rigours of the European Tour. It may be a quick reset in the lap of family, but at the nearby familiar course, there's practice and preparation with coach Gurbaaz Mann to deal with the long stretch ahead.Le Golf National awaits next week for the Open de France at the elegant-sounding Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines, under the suburban skies of Paris. There are boxes to tick, and a weekend wish, but the mind travels to the rolling hills of Kasugai Country Club, where the Asian Games competition starts on Sept 30."I played in Japan last year so I have a very fair idea how the golf courses are," he says. "We already have the course mapped out in detail, and the yardages. And I think playing on the DP World Tour has polished my game so I feel ready to tackle the course.""It's rained a lot there recently so the course will definitely be softer. We are expecting ideal weather. Besides, I'm pretty much accustomed to playing in such conditions, I've been playing in the rain four weeks out of the past eight," the 29-year-old adds.Japan golf connoisseur Jeev Milkha Singh has advised the Games-bound golfers to work on their short game, and Yuvraj doesn't need a reminder. "Last year, Jeev sir and I played together at International Series Japan, we stayed close by and had a few meals and he helped me a lot with understanding Japanese conditions in general, and, him being a legend in Japan, he's told me a few things about how to play the courses and I've taken his words to heart. "And what about his rapport with the other members of the team, Saptak Talwar and Veer Ahlawat? "It's actually pretty good because we've played a lot of amateur golf together. We've also played junior golf together. Veer is a class senior to us, and he had a European Tour card last season. Saptak also plays on the second-tier Tour so we all have the experience. We are from the same age group so it makes it easier to talk about things around the course. I feel very comfortable going back to Japan, there's a high chance we will bring home a medal."Part of that confidence stems from the Euro grind, of course. "We play in 6 degrees when it's raining and the wind is howling at 40 kms/hr. There is a very big difference between just playing golf, and playing competitive golf in those battling conditions. So I think coping with that sort of mentality makes me more gritty, it makes me a more aggressive player when it comes to favourable conditions, probably like Japan."After winning seven PGTI tournaments in 2025, Yuvraj earned the pathway to the DP World Tour, and it has been a tough initiation. "When you go from a pool to an ocean, it makes a lot of difference. You are swimming with the fishes, and then suddenly you are swimming with the whales and sharks. So you got to grow and the transition takes time, but it's definitely all worth it. I will go to Q-School if things don't go my way. That's the reason I'm playing the sport.That's the dream," says the No. 202 in the Race to Dubai rankings."I've realized that it is important to address other things apart from swinging the club, be it the mental part or the rehab part. I've learned to be a better athlete, not just be a better golfer."A missed cut sometimes doesn't show your gains. "At the last tournament (Omega European Masters in Switzerland), I made seven-over on the first day, but in the second round, I shot 5-under. I played phenomenal golf. Not making the cut didn't really take a lot off my confidence, but somewhere, it does affect you. But your team helps you, and I have always believed in myself. Missing cuts are like making bogeys. You will make bogeys, you will make birdies. And the sooner you accept it, I think the better golfer you will be."
Article Summary: Yuvraj Sandhu will be taking the long route to Japan for the Asian Games. The 29-year-old is the No. 202 in the Race to Dubai rankings. Yuvraj won seven PGTI tournaments in 2025, earning the pathway to the DP World Tour.

Article Title: Chess Olympiad Round 2: How Nihal Sarin saved India's day amid Gukesh's historic drop in rating points
Article Text:
Nihal Sarin (on right) saves India's day at Round 2 of Chess Olympiad (Photo by Rafal Oleksiewicz for FIDE)

D Gukesh draws his Round 2 game (Photo by Rafal Oleksiewicz for FIDE)

How Nihal Sarin saved India's day

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Indian women's team registers comfortable win, opponents for Round 3 revealed

NEW DELHI: The current world champion, Dommaraju Gukesh, was on Board 1 facing all the top-rated opponents during India's gold-clinching campaign in Budapest at the 2024 Chess Olympiad. Besides the team, Gukesh won an individual gold too, boosting his overall confidence ahead of the Championship challenge against China's Ding Liren. If that was the highest point of Gukesh's Olympiad journey, Round 2 of the 46th edition of the Chess Olympiad brought the lowest, as the 20-year-old Chennai grandmaster fell below 2700 rating after his draw against Indonesia's International Master (IM) Satria Duta Cahaya on Thursday in Samarkand, Uzbekistan.With Arjun Erigaisi taking a rest after his loss against Thai IM Prin Laohawirapap on the opening day of the tournament and Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa taking his designated Board 1 this time, Gukesh once again took Board 3 in India's match against Indonesia.The game itself, however, was a long, patient battle rather than a disaster.Playing black against a much lower-rated opponent, Gukesh went into a Sicilian setup and spent the middlegame manoeuvring, with his knights hopping back and forth, both kings tucked away, neither side finding a real breakthrough.Around the 40-move mark, pieces started coming off the board, and by the endgame Gukesh was left with a queen and knight against Cahaya's queen and knight, with roughly level chances.Needing a win to protect his rating and unable to find one, Gukesh eventually used his queen to give a string of checks around Cahaya's king, a "perpetual check", which forced the draw by repetition.It was a safe result, but not the kind expected from a reigning world champion against a 2412-rated opponent.Gukesh had started this Olympiad at 2703 and now sits at 2699.5, dropping below the 2700 mark for the first time since he first crossed it back in 2022.There is a general feeling that the Board 3 assignment could cut both ways for him. He won't run into the strongest opposition every round, but any slip against a lower-rated player carries outsized risk to his rating, exactly as it did on Thursday.With three of India's four boards ending in draws, it was Nihal Sarin who kept the team's campaign on track, beating Indonesia's Arif Abdul Hafiz. Even though for a large stretch of the game, that outcome looked far from certain.Playing white and the Sicilian Defence, Nihal castled queenside and launched a kingside attack with g4 and g5. However, Hafiz countered well, winning pawns and creating serious threats around Nihal’s king. After 22...Qxc2+, Black appeared to have taken control, while Nihal was also running dangerously low on time.The turning point came with 28.Rxc6+!, a bold rook sacrifice. Instead of trying to recover his material, Nihal chose to expose the black king. After 28...Kxc6, he continued with Qxe4+ and Qxb4, bringing his queen into the attack. A series of checks then forced the black king around the board, while Hafiz’s clock continued to fall.By 37.Nc5+, Black had no way out and resigned.It was a scrappy, double-edged fight rather than a clean demolition, but exactly the kind of gritty win India needed to avoid an upset.Elsewhere in the Indonesia match, Praggnanandhaa, back on Board 1 after Wednesday's rest day, drew with Susanto Megaranto, while Vidit Santosh Gujrathi also settled for a draw on Board 4 against Nayaka Budhidharma.With Nihal's win as the difference-maker, India closed out the match 2.5-1.5 to stay unbeaten through two rounds.With Koneru Humpy taking a rest day, the 2025 Women's World Cup winner Divya Deshmukh made her first appearance in this edition of Women's Olympiad.Nevertheless, the women's team had a far more comfortable outing, brushing aside Finland 3.5-0.5. Vaishali Rameshbabu drew her game, but Divya, Vantika Agrawal and Savitha Shri all won to seal a dominant scoreline.India will look to keep the winning streak going on Friday, when the men's team takes on Italy, and the women face Greece.
Article Summary: Current world champion Dommaraju Gukesh was on Board 1 during India's gold- clinching campaign in Budapest at the 2024 Chess Olympiad. The 20-year-old Chennai grandmaster fell below 2700 rating after his draw against Indonesia's International Master (IM) Satria Duta Cahaya on Thursday.

Article Title: Despite loss, India’s teqball story only just beginning
Article Text:
Representational image of teqball. (AP Photo/Aaron Favila)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nagoya: India’s Asian Games journey began in rather muted fashion at the Higashi Sports Centre here at 4:06 pm. There was no fanfare and barely any indication that history was being made. A volunteer holding a placard was the only sign that an Asian Games event was under way.The sport was teqball — a little-known combination of football and table tennis — and India’s men’s doubles pair of Declan Gonsalves and Mohamed Anas went down fighting 10-12, 8-12 to Vietnam and 4-12, 7-12 to South Korea.Their campaign ended, but for India’s small community of about 180 teqball athletes, the day marked the beginning of something bigger. One of six sports making its Asian Games debut, teqball is played on a curved table resembling a table-tennis table. The sport originated in Hungary and is only 12 years old. In India, it has been around for barely four years.That hasn’t stopped a small band of ‘teqers’ from chasing their passion.On Thursday, six Indians in the stands cheered Gonsalves and Anas. Among them were India’s deputy chef de mission and former shooting stalwart Anjali Bhagwat, and Declan’s parents Derek and Deborah Gonsalves, who had flown in from Mumbai to witness a slice of history.Anas will get another opportunity when he teams up with Quimcy Dsouza in the mixed doubles. Quimcy will also compete in the women’s singles.For the first generation of Indian teqers, the last four years have involved as much explaining as playing.“All the four years I have been playing the sport, I’ve only been explaining what it is. But the Asian Games is a huge opportunity for us,” said Bengaluru-based Quimcy, who quit her job in Mumbai and moved to the city to set up a teqball facility.She was drawn to the sport after watching videos of former Brazil football star Ronaldinho playing it on social media.“I started playing the sport around the time the last Asian Games was held. Back then, if somebody told me I would be playing in the Asian Games this year, I wouldn’t have believed it. This is a dream come true,” said Quimcy, one of a group of self-taught athletes who have now taken on coaching roles as well.Nihar Shah, technical director of Teqball India, believes the sport is beginning to find a foothold, particularly in the Northeast, where several players have a background in sepaktakraw.“While it’s still new, there has been a lot of interest in it lately. We hope the Asian Games appearance of the three athletes gives it a further push,” Shah said.
Article Summary: India's men's doubles pair of Declan Gonsalves and Mohamed Anas went down fighting 10-12, 8-12 to Vietnam. Teqball is played on a curved table resembling a table-tennis table. The sport originated in Hungary and is only 12 years old.

Article Title: For women’s cricket, Asiad a ‘teaser’ before 2028 LA Olympics opportunity
Article Text:
Harmanpreet Kaur

China out without playing

Nagoya: India start favourites to win the women’s cricket gold here, but Harmanpreet Kaur and her team have a bigger prize on their mind — the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where cricket will return to the Games after 128 years. Cricket made its only previous Olympic appearance at Paris in 1900, when Great Britain and France were the only teams competing. As the defending champions begin their campaign against hosts Japan in the quarterfinals at Korogi Athletic Park in Nisshin City on Friday, head coach Amol Muzumdar said he saw the Asian Games as a teaser for the Olympic assignment.“This is a great teaser towards the Olympic quest for the Indian women’s team. We are getting used to certain things at the Asian Games. Touring to a different part of the world for this — we’ll do the same in LA — will be a different experience for most of us,” Muzumdar said on Thursday.Harmanpreet echoed the thoughts of her coach, saying the team would approach the tournament with the same mindset that helped them win gold on their Asian Games debut in Hangzhou in 2022. “As a team we are really looking forward to the Olympics and (here) we will go with the same mindset and approach like the last time,” she said.For now, though, the immediate target is to retain the Asian Games crown. “We respect every opponent, we start from zero and whenever India plays the aim is to always compete for the gold,” Muzumdar said.It was heartbreak for the Chinese women’s cricket team as their quarterfinal against Bangladesh was abandoned without a ball being bowled.The match, which was initially delayed, was eventually called off, sending Bangladesh into the semifinals on basis of being the higher-ranked team. They will next face the winner of Friday’s India-Japan quarterfinal.Pakistan also made the last four after surviving a scare before beating Thailand by three wickets in a low-scoring contest.

Article Title: Rowers head into Asian Games hoping to peak when it matters most
Article Text:
Representational Photo

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Fewer sport test the limits of human endurance, power and stamina as rowing does. A marathoner might expend around 3,000 kilocalories over a 42.2km course, but he or she does so at a sub-optimal level, meaning the rate of burn is about 13 kilocalories per minute.In comparison, an oarsman may require only around 140 kilocalories to complete a 2km race lasting 5.5 to 7.5 minutes. The total energy demand may be far lower, but the intensity is much higher, reaching about 20 kilocalories per minute.While the distance runner has to tap into his reserves over a sustained period for a prolonged effort, the rower draws on 85 per cent of his muscles with each stroke, as opposed to 50 percent in the case of running. Then you add the unpredictable: the elements.The key element, though, is the human in the boat.The Indian team’s preparation in this Asian Games cycle has received a large dose of sports science, thanks to the arrival of Australian Antony Patterson at the Army Rowing Node. Conversations are peppered with phrases like heart rate, prognostic percentage and living document. The women rowers, meanwhile, have found corporate backing in recent years.Under Patterson, there has also been a fundamental shift in selecting team combinations, perhaps necessitated by the new rule that countries can compete in only 10 events. So, whereas in the past top rowers entered their strongest events, this time events with maximum chance of winning a medal have been identified and combinations decided accordingly.But while the preparation has been science-driven and meticulous, a positive dope test and the ministry’s decision to axe two women’s teams had dented the squad’s morale. A fourth-place finish in the lightweight double scull at last month’s World Championships and a recent mind-training session in Pune seems to have revived their confidence.Time, then, for India’s rowers to translate meticulous preparation into medals.# Riding the tide of hopeHaving won three medals (one silver and two bronze) in each of the past two editions of the Asian Games, Indian sailors will be looking to add to their tally when they set out on the water in Gamagori City.Vishnu Saravanan (ILCA-7), Nethra Kumanan (ILCA-6), Harshita Tomar (49erFX) and debutant Manu Francis (49er) give India a chance to improve on its best-ever showing at the continental event.India’s main rivals are expected to be China, hosts Japan and Malaysia.
Article Summary: The Indian team’s preparation in this Asian Games cycle has received a large dose of sports science, thanks to the arrival of Australian Antony Patterson at the Army Rowing Node. The women rowers, meanwhile, have found corporate backing in recent years. A fourth-place finish in the lightweight double scull at the World Championships and a recent mind-training session in Pune seems to have revived their confidence.

Article Title: New Zealand star's India series participation in doubt after freak injury
Article Text:
New Zealand's Rachin Ravindra (AP photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Rachin Ravindra's availability for New Zealand's upcoming five-match T20I series against India has been thrown into doubt after he dislocated his right shoulder during a promotional shoot in Auckland.The all-rounder suffered the injury on Wednesday (September 16) while attempting a diving catch during filming with Sky. Ravindra landed awkwardly on a safety mat, according to New Zealand Performance Manager Mike Sandle.An initial examination by medical specialists on Friday (September 18) found no major structural damage. However, the 25-year-old's recovery period will depend on how he responds during the early phase of his rehabilitation.The T20I series against India is scheduled to begin on October 22, leaving Ravindra with just over a month to recover. His availability for the series, however, remains uncertain."It was a really unfortunate injury," Sandle said. "We're gutted for Rachin and our key priority is making sure he recovers well and gets back on the field as soon as he can."As with all commercial shoots involving our players, the activities were agreed in advance by all parties, with appropriate safety measures in place.It was a bit of a freak accident, and we'll continue to review our processes around events like this in the future."New Zealand are also keen to avoid taking unnecessary risks with Ravindra given the packed Test calendar that awaits the team over the next six months.Head coach Rob Walter said the focus would be on ensuring the player makes a full recovery rather than pushing him back prematurely."With a heavy schedule of Test cricket in the next six months, we don't want to rush Rachin back sooner than we need to. He's in great hands in terms of his rehab and we look forward to welcoming him back soon," Walter said.New Zealand are due to name their T20I squad for the India series early next week, with Ravindra's rehabilitation progress likely to be a key factor in determining his availability.
Article Summary: Rachin Ravindra dislocated his right shoulder during a promotional shoot in Auckland. The all-rounder suffered the injury while attempting a diving catch during filming with Sky. Initial examination by medical specialists on Friday (September 18) found no major structural damage. The T20I series against India is scheduled to begin on October 22.

Article Title: Asian Games: BCCI books separate accommodation for men's cricket team, women stay in Games facilities
Article Text:
India's players celebrate the wicket of Afghanistan's Sediqullah Atal during the third and final T20I cricket match between India and Afghanistan, in New Delhi. (PTI Photo)

'Asiad gold as important as any other title'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

'Match against Japan was ICC chair's idea'

NEW DELHI: As reports of a crisis over the accommodation arrangements start coming in from the Asian Games in Japan, it has emerged that the Indian cricket board (BCCI) has arranged its own accommodation for the men's cricket team."BCCI has arranged its own arrangement for the men’s team since the contingent is much bigger than the permissible number of members because of the size of the support staff. We don’t want to segregate the men’s team during the tournament," BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia told TOI."The women’s team is staying in the facilities provided by the organising committee since the size of the contingent is within the permissible number of 20 members," he added.However, Saikia insisted that the BCCI has faith in the local organisation committee to provide satisfactory on-ground facilities at the match venue despite reports of other Asian cricket boards raising objections about the quality of the ground. "We fully trust the organising committee to give the best facilities. This is a big event and I am sure they will do what is required. I'll be reaching there on Oct 1. Only then I can give you a clear picture of the circumstances," he added.There have been contrasting views in Indian cricket circles about the board's decision to send a full-strength T20I team to the Asian Games, which coincides with the start of the preparations for next year's ODI World Cup as India are slated to play an ODI series against West Indies at home. India will have at least seven first-choice ODI players playing at the Asian Games. Interestingly, India won the gold medal at the last Asian Games in 2023 with a second-string team as the premier players were held back to prepare for the 2023 ODI World Cup.Saikia asserted that the board's decision was based on the realisation of the value of an Asian Games gold medal. "We are eyeing a gold medal which is very important. We all know India can field three strong teams at a time. We see Asian Games as a very important assignment which can’t be given secondary treatment. That’s why our full-strength team including Bumrah and regular captain Iyer is going. An Asian Games gold is as important as any other big tournament," Saikia stated."I wasn't the secretary when the last Asian Games happened. So, I can't comment on it," he added.The BCCI also announced a T20I match against Japan on September 22 to celebrate 75 years of diplomatic relations between India and Japan. Saikia revealed that the idea of the match was initiated by ICC chairman Jay Shah. "It’s the initiative of ICC chairman Jay Shah who wants to take cricket to every nook and corner of the world. He made me sit with my Japanese counterpart during the last ICC meet in Edinburgh in July this year. Japan is a country where cricket is growing gradually. Mr. Shah took this initiative and we agreed to the idea," said Saikia.
Article Summary: BCCI has arranged its own arrangement for the men’s team since the contingent is much bigger than the permissible number of members because of the size of the support staff. BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia said the decision was based on the realisation of the value of an Asian Games gold medal. Article Title: 'Fifteen days is a long time': BCCI plays wait-and-watch on Ajit Agarkar's future
Article Text:
Devajit Saikia, Ajit Agarkar

'Lot of time & processes for BCCI to come under Sports Act'

Promotion & relegation introduced for domestic umpires

'IPL to start from last week of March'

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BGT Test on in Ranchi

The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) secretary Devajit Saikia on Friday offered no clear answers on the future of men's selection committee chief Ajit Agarkar but said that "15 days is a long time in the world of cricket.""We still have fifteen days to go. Fifteen days is a long time in the world of cricket. We will take a decision in appropriate time and we will let you know about it. Today, there was no discussion on any individual,” Saikia said after the conclusion of the Annual General Meeting at the BCCI headquarters.This comes after BCCI vice-president Rajeev Shukla said earlier in the day that the board has authorised its office-bearers to take a decision on the future of the men's senior selection committee headed by Ajit Agarkar."Arun Singh Dhumal, Majumdar retain IPL governing council posts; AGM authorises office-bearers to take a decision on selectors," Shukla said after attending the meeting at the BCCI headquarters.BCCI president Mithun Manhas, vice-president Rajeev Shukla, secretary Devajit Saikia, Bengal Cricket Association president Sourav Ganguly, and Jharkhand State Cricket Association secretary Saurabh Tiwary were among the officials present at the AGM.Agarkar was appointed chairman of the men's senior selection committee in July 2023, and his contract is scheduled to end next month.Meanwhile, Saikia also said the BCCI has begun appointing a new five-member junior selection committee. "We have received a very large number of applicants, so we are shortlisting it, and once the shortlisting is completed, then we will give it to our cricket committee, who will be the competent authority to select the selectors for the junior selection committee, so that process is going on, and we are trying to complete it within the next 10-15 days time, to constitute the junior selection committee, because all five selectors' tenure is going to be over very soon," Saikia said.Saikia clarified that there was plenty of time before the BCCI would come under the National Sports Governance (NSG) Act. The Supreme Court recently asked the BCCI and its state associations to clarify their position following multiple litigations involving various associations either for minor changes in their constitution or disputes arising from factionalism.Saikia clarified that the BCCI was not averse to coming under the new Sports Act, provided the government completes a few processes."So, regarding the Sports Act, our stand is very clear. There are a lot of things which are yet to be done by the concerned authority; once those exercises are completed, and once BCCI comes under the Sports Act, a particular notification has to be issued to make it a designated sport. Till that time, we are not supposed to do anything. Whenever that notification comes, we will immediately spring into action. We will then do our work as per the new sports rules," Saikia said."We are paying Rs 3,000 crore tax annually to the government. Unlike other sports federations, we don't take any government funding. Hence, cricket cannot be treated as a 'designated sport' under the National Sports Governance Act 2025," Saikia pointed out.Saikia said that the BCCI will introduce a system of promotion and relegation for umpires in domestic cricket, with 10 umpires being promoted and 10 relegated after every season."All the umpires’ postings will be as per merit. We have an assessing team under the umpires’ board. They will be given assignments according to their merit - whether it is knockouts or important games. After every season, there will be a system of relegation and upgradation. Ten umpires at the end of every season will be promoted, and ten will be relegated. This will make them very alert throughout the season, and that will ultimately help the game of cricket because some players’ futures depend on decisions of the umpires. They have to be very competent and alert," he stated.As reported by TOI on Friday, Saikia confirmed that the BCCI had decided to increase the pay of domestic match referees and umpires from the upcoming season. "There was no revision of fees of the umpires for almost ten years from 2017-18. Earlier there were four categories - A+, A, B, C; now we have restricted it to A, B, C, D. Their per-day fees have been enhanced substantially. We have also enhanced the fee structure of the match referees," Saikia said.Saikia revealed that "IPL-2027 will start from the last week of March." He said that the BCCI has grand plans to celebrate its 100th anniversary (in 2028) and the IPL's 20th anniversary next year. "In Dec 2028, we will complete 100 years of the BCCI, so we will do centenary celebrations from Dec 2027 for one year. The IPL, which will start from March next year, will have its 20th edition. We have discussed that it should be done in a grand way. We have also seen a presentation (on it) after the AGM," Saikia said.Saikia also informed that Shubhadeep Ghosh, who is India's fielding coach, has been appointed on a short-term basis.Meanwhile, former India batter Saurabh Tiwary, currently the secretary of the Jharkhand State Cricket Association (JSCA), rubbished reports of Ranchi being replaced as a venue for next year’s Border-Gavaskar Trophy due to poor weather conditions. The marquee five-Test series will begin on Jan 21 in Nagpur, with Chennai, Guwahati, Ranchi and Ahmedabad hosting the other four Tests."There is no change in the venue. If anybody has to write to the BCCI about it, it should be me and I have not written it," Tiwary told the media.“There are six to seven months left (for the Ranchi Test). We don't have any such request or proposal that there are some issues regarding the Ranchi Test,” Saikia said.
Article Summary: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) secretary Devajit Saikia on Friday offered no clear answers on the future of men's selection committee chief Ajit Agarkar. "We will take a decision in appropriate time and we will let you know about it. Today, there was no discussion on any individual," he said after the conclusion of the Annual General Meeting at the BCCI headquarters.Saikia said that the BCCi will introduce a system of promotion and relegation for umpires in domestic cricket.

Article Title: After getting just one international in 2026-27 season, MCA asks BCCI to allot more matches to Wankhede Stadium
Article Text:
Groundsmen work on the pitch ahead of 2nd test cricket match between India and New Zealand, at Wankhede stadium in Mumbai. (PTI File Photo)

MCA seeks Under-17 girls' tournament

MUMBAI: The Mumbai Cricket Association has requested the Board of Control for Cricket in India ( BCCI ) to allot more international matches to the Wankhede Stadium in future schedules, while also seeking to be informed before matches are awarded to other venues in Mumbai.The request was made during the 95th Annual General Meeting (AGM) of the BCCI at its headquarters on the Wankhede Stadium premises. MCA secretary Unmesh Khanvilkar submitted a letter, a copy of which is with TOI, putting forward the association's demands.The MCA's request comes after Wankhede was allotted only one international match in India's 2026-27 home season. The stadium will host the third and final ODI between India and Zimbabwe on January 9 next year.The MCA, which celebrated the Wankhede Stadium's 50th anniversary in January 2025, has pointed out that the venue is a permanent Test Centre and has asked the BCCI to consider giving it more international matches.“The MCA sincerely thanks the BCCI for the international matches allotted to Mumbai over the years and for its continued confidence in the Association's hosting capabilities. As the Wankhede Stadium is a permanent Test Centre with a proud history of successfully staging marquee international fixtures, MCA would be grateful if the BCCI could consider allotting a greater number of international matches to the venue in future programmes.We remain committed to providing the highest standards of facilities and match operations for players, officials, and spectators alike,” Khanvilkar has written.The MCA has also asked the BCCI to inform the association before awarding matches to stadiums and venues located within its jurisdiction, which includes Mumbai.The request comes after the BCCI announced a couple of days ago that the 2027 Women's Premier League will be held at the Brabourne Stadium, which is operated by the Cricket Club of India, from January 14 to February 27. Brabourne Stadium is located around 750 metres from Wankhede.The International Cricket Council has also recently awarded the inaugural Women's T20 Champions Trophy matches to Brabourne Stadium. The tournament is scheduled to be held from February 14 to 28.The MCA said being informed in advance would help it deal with queries from its members and other stakeholders and coordinate with the organisations involved in staging matches in Mumbai.“The MCA would be grateful if, as a matter of courtesy, the Association could be kept informed whenever matches are scheduled at stadiums or venues located within its jurisdiction. Such communication would assist MCA in addressing queries from its members and stakeholders and would help foster smooth coordination and cooperation among all concerned,” the MCA has stated in its letter.The MCA has also asked the BCCI to introduce an Under-17 girls' tournament in its domestic cricket calendar.The BCCI currently conducts a Girls Under-15 tournament, with the next age-group competitions starting at the Under-19 level.“The MCA requests the BCCI to consider introducing a structured Under-17 Girls Cricket Tournament at the national level. Such a tournament would provide an important competitive platform for young female cricketers, strengthen the talent development pathway, and further support the growth of women's cricket across the country,” Khanvilkar has stated in his letter.“We request the Board to give due consideration to the above matters and look forward to a positive response,” Khanvilkar concluded in his letter.
Article Summary: Wankhede was allotted only one international match in India's 2026-27 home season. The MCA has also asked the BCCI to introduce an Under-17 girls' tournament in its domestic cricket calendar. MCA secretary Unmesh Khanvilkar submitted a letter, a copy of which is with TOI, putting forward the demands.

Article Title: BCCI to take call on Ajit Agarkar's future after AGM authorisation, confirms Rajeev Shukla
Article Text:
BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia, BCCI president Mithun Manhas, and BCCI vice president Rajeev Shukla (left), Ajit Agarkar

The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has authorised its office-bearers to take a decision on the future of the men's senior selection committee headed by Ajit Agarkar, vice-president Rajeev Shukla confirmed after the Board's 95th Annual General Meeting (AGM) in Mumbai on Friday."Arun Singh Dhumal, Majumdar retain IPL governing council posts; AGM authorises office-bearers to take a decision on selectors," Shukla said after attending the meeting at the BCCI headquarters.BCCI president Mithun Manhas, vice-president Rajeev Shukla, secretary Devajit Saikia, Bengal Cricket Association president Sourav Ganguly, and Jharkhand State Cricket Association secretary Saurabh Tiwary were among the officials present at the AGM.Agarkar was appointed chairman of the men's senior selection committee in July 2023, and his contract is scheduled to end next month.If his tenure ends without an extension, the BCCI will not be able to appoint a new chairman immediately. The Board will first have to advertise the position and then conduct interviews before naming a replacement, making the appointment process likely to take some time.As reported earlier by TimesofIndia.com, former India wicketkeeper-batter Parthiv Patel has emerged as a strong contender to replace Agarkar if the BCCI and the current chairman do not agree on an extension.If appointed, Parthiv would become the most experienced member of the current selection panel with 25 Test appearances. The other members are SS Das (23 Tests), RP Singh (14 Tests), Pragyan Ojha (24 Tests) and Ajay Ratra (6 Tests).The selectors announced India's squads for the upcoming home white-ball series against West Indies earlier this week. Their next major responsibility will be selecting India's Test and India 'A' squads for the tour of New Zealand in October and November.India will play five T20Is, five ODIs and two Tests against New Zealand, while India 'A' will play three unofficial Tests against New Zealand 'A' in a shadow tour ahead of the two-match Test series.
Article Summary: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has authorised its office- bearers to take a decision on the future of the men's senior selection committee. Ajit Agarkar's contract is scheduled to end next month. If his tenure ends without an extension, the BCCI will not be able to appoint a new chairman immediately.

NEW DELHI: Former India cricketer Parthiv Patel has emerged as a strong candidate to replace Ajit Agarkar as the men's senior selection committee chairman if the incumbent and the BCCI don't reach an extension agreement.TimesofIndia.com has learnt that Parthiv's name has been circulating in Indian cricket's power corridors for the last six months when key figures were preparing for life after Agarkar. While an extension for the Mumbaikar wasn't off the table back then, a strong cosensus had been reached on Parthiv as the possible successor for the top job.If everything falls into place, Parthiv will be the most senior member of the panel with 25 Tests. SS Das played 23 Tests, RP Singh made 14 appearances while Pragyan Ojha and Ajay Ratra had 24 and 6 caps, respectively. The Indian cricket board has remained tight-lipped on the matter but clarity could be expected in the coming weeks.Agarkar picked the squads for the ODIs and T20Is against West Indies, and the Rest of India team for the Irani Cup and strong murmurs suggest this could well have been his last selection meeting.The former India cricketer attended the India-Afghanistan T20Is in Delhi, accompanied by selectors RP and Ratra. The second game of the series was also attended by ICC Chairman Jay Shah, BCCI President Mithun Manhas and Vice-President Rajeev Shukla.After the Annual General Meeting (AGM) in Mumbai on Friday, Shukla was brief on the topic, "AGM authorises office-bearers to take a decision on selectors."Agarkar recently missed the high-profile review meeting attended by the Indian cricket board's top brass, head coach Gautam Gambhir, Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill, T20I captain Shreyas Iyer, CoE head VVS Laxman. While the BCCI Secretary Devajit Saikia downplayed the chief selector's absence saying he was out of town, those tracking developments believe it "doesn't add up"."You had everyone available there. It's not every day you get the key figures of Indian cricket under the same roof. Head coach travelled from Delhi, Laxman travelled, and Gill and Iyer both juggled their commitments. Mithun Manhas travelled too. So it was a bit strange that the chairman of the men's senior selection committee wasn't there when key issues were on the table.It just doesn't add up," said a source close to developments.Indian cricket is staring at a crucial 12 months in the build-up to the 2027 edition of the ODI World Cup and the ongoing World Test Championship cycle. While a section believes continuity with Agarkar is need of the hour, there are some influential voices keen to hand the reigns to Parthiv.The former India keeper is currently serving as assistant and batting coach at Gujarat Titans and commentating when his schedule permits. It is understood that Parthiv was likely to get a bigger role in the IPL franchise from the next cycle but if the selector role materialises, GT will probably have to explore different options.

India Women rewrote their T20I record books with a crushing eight-wicket victory over Japan, completing a 58-run chase in just five overs to register their biggest win by balls remaining. The defending champions finished the quarter-final with 90 balls to spare, surpassing their previous mark of 84 balls against Thailand in 2022.The record-breaking win at Korogi Sports Park in Nisshin on Friday also sent India into the semi-finals of the 2026 Asian Games, where they will face Bangladesh on Sunday for a place in the medal match.After winning the toss and opting to field, India’s bowlers bundled Japan out for 57 in 19.5 overs. Japan lost wickets at regular intervals and were unable to post a challenging total.India’s chase was swift and emphatic. Shafali Verma smashed an unbeaten 40 off just 15 balls, including four boundaries and two sixes, to put India firmly in control.India lost Gunalan Kamalini for a duck and Bharti Fulmali for six, but Japan could not capitalise on those breakthroughs. Richa Ghosh joined Shafali and scored an unbeaten 12 off six balls.With one run needed, Shafali finished the contest in style, launching Shimako Kato over long-on for a six. India reached 59/2 in five overs, sealing the win with 90 deliveries remaining.India’s record victory sets up a semi-final clash against Bangladesh, while Pakistan will take on Sri Lanka in the other last-four encounter on Sunday.
